mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 4% for two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days due to tightened discount rates affecting future equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains >4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window following the trigger, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically different from the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly UNRATE falls below 3.5% for three consecutive months, it indicates labor market softening that coincides with higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days as investors anticipate corporate cost-cutting and improved earnings prospects.
failure_condition: In 80% of similar labor-weakening regimes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.2).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both GDPC1 (goods demand) and HOUST (housing demand) over the prior 10 months predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return in the next 5 trading days as a dual recovery in consumption and housing supports equity risk premia.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous 10-month average AND HOUST > previous 10-month average
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is not significantly above the prior 5-day average (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 10% in a single month followed by a month of above-trend employment (PAYEMS > 150k) predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as excess supply of goods and labor suppresses growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > INDPRO previous month +10% AND PAYEMS > 150000
regime_hint: supply shock followed by labor recovery
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive in >70% of similar events (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for four consecutive months, it signals accommodative policy sustaining equity risk premia, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in PAYEMS (employment) by over 20k in a single month followed by two months of declining inflation (CPIAUCSL < 250) predicts a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days as labor market strength offsets inflationary concerns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > PAYEMS previous month +20000 AND CPIAUCSL < 250 for 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: In regimes where UNRATE > 5% and FEDFUNDS > 4% simultaneously for at least 3 months, the S&P 500 exhibits a negative 20-day forward return as high labor costs and tight policy suppress growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% AND FEDFUNDS > 4% for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive policy regime
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in >50% of such regimes (empirical frequency).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in GDPC1 (goods demand) of 15% in the prior quarter followed by a sustained drop in RSAFS (retail sales) of 8% in the current month predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as indicators of weakening demand pressure equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < GDPC1 previous quarter -15% AND RSAFS < RSAFS previous month -8%
regime_hint: demand contraction in retail and industrial sectors
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is positive in >80% of analogous contraction events (walk-forward validation).
